parts.problem_md:
The Venn diagram shows information about the number of students in a class who like apples ($A$) and bananas ($B$).

![qp5a-0580-33-paper-3-may-2020-cie-igcse-maths](assets/016-qp5a-0580-33-paper-3-may-2020-cie-igcse-maths.png)

i) Work out the number of students in the class.

[1]

ii) Work out the number of students who like bananas.

[1]

iii) Work out  `n open parentheses A union B close parentheses`.

[1]

iv) How many more students like apples than like bananas?

[1]
parts.solution_md:
(i) *Add up all the numbers in the Venn diagram. *

*12 + 8 + 7 + 4 = 31 *

**31**** ****[1]**

** **(ii) *Add together the two numbers in the **B** circle. *

*8 + 7 = 15 *

**15** **[1]**

** **(iii) `n open parentheses A union B close parentheses`* means the number of students who like apples **or **bananas.*

> *Add together the three numbers from inside both circles. *

*12 + 8 + 7 = 27 *

**27**** ****[1]**

** **(iv) *Add together the numbers in the **A **circle to work out how many students like apples, then subtract the number of students who like bananas, 15. *

*(12 + 8) - 15 = 5 *

**5** **[1]**
